g_img_needs: Verdicts bound to the file sha256; any code fix makes a new hash and needs a QA re-confirm (the vase clamp is the model case)

Allowed 0-token code fixes: uniform downscale, translate/gap, interior alpha clamp, global linear exposure gain <= 10% (logged k), re-matte from the raw. Forbidden: non-uniform scale, warp, retouch/paint, recolour (P4, G2.11). Each verified by a rebuild from the raw (alpha IoU >= 0.995, mean RGB diff <= 5 apart from the declared operation)
Colour: lit side on a material mask (stone, fabric, ceramic), not the whole product; primary dE00 vs the SKU lit side <= 3; the absolute window as a flag
Geometry: proportion between ellipse centres with one fixed tool; a single-viewpoint check (both end ellipses consistent with one camera; edge-on b/a <= 0.08 where the house angle is level)

Material per category: waffle - one period peak, spread <= 10% after perspective, fringe/cell +-20% vs the SKU; stone - pore density x0.5-x2 of the SKU photo, same tool; ceramic - crease spacing +-25% vs the SKU (round-1 D4)

Alpha: interior 255, border 0, no specks; edge colour vs a clean edge; fibre/fringe matte: in the outer fringe band >= 50% of between-thread gaps at alpha <= 0.5 and tip loss <= 0.5 cell vs the raw, checked on paper and dark
C2 with the round-1 clarification (house elements not counted unless measured within spec; a deviation toward a supplier's choice counts)
C2b: high-pass NCC for non-periodic surfaces; tile-repeat autocorrelation for periodic textures

House angle measured and reported (texture foreshortening for flat textiles, end ellipses for cylinders, rim ellipse for vessels); a deviation goes to the designer / D5, not a fidelity fail, unless it moves toward a supplier composition
Inputs from render-agent per job: raw and no-bg files, the palette used, code-fix parameters, final sha256, reference sheet by card index
p1_lessons: P1 works when the product is already faithful in our frame and large enough (vase ~260 px in the base): nano keeps scale; the room drifts a little warm and loses unsold fill - acceptable, designer eye
Small products: a loose base inflates them (lamp x1.8-2.05); a tiny base (100x125) lets the model invent the room

Arithmetic conflict: native 2K at 50% fill needs the product >= 1024 px in the 4K raw, i.e. >= 22% of the base height. The ed4 lamp (75 px) would need a base <= ~270x340, which contradicts QA's 400x500 anchor base. For products under ~25 cm, G4.16 + native 2K cannot both hold from today's frames: owner decision (accept native >= 1360x1700, or 35-40% fill, or a dedicated close-up render)
Textile P1: nano kept the frame's own throw; run P1 only after P2 passes, with the true-scale fabric square and an explicit replace line
Run P1 only on materials whose P2 route is proven (ceramic, textile; not stone yet)
Always measure against an anchor on the raw before any crop (unchanged from round 1)
